SEPA PAYMENT FILE VALIDATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Will your bank accept this SEPA payment file?

Paste or drop a SEPA credit transfer file (pain.001 XML) and get every error with its line number: malformed XML, invalid IBANs, transaction count and control sum, execution dates on a weekend or TARGET2 holiday, non-euro amounts and characters outside the SEPA set. After a hand edit, rebuild the counts and control sums in one click and download the corrected file.

The file is read in this browser tab and never leaves your device. Account numbers are masked to their last four characters in the report. Independent of the EPC and of every bank. The rules are read from memory of the public EPC and ISO 20022 documents; no bank's own validator was available when this was built.

1. Your payment file

Usually an .xml file exported from accounting, payroll or ERP software for upload to online banking: it starts with <Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.03"> (or .09).

Choose a file or paste the text, then click Validate.

Rebuild the counts and control sums

    The model, and what it leaves out

    • Structure: Document → CstmrCdtTrfInitn → one GrpHdr and one or more PmtInf blocks, each with CdtTrfTxInf transactions. Versions pain.001.001.03 and .09 are read; others are flagged.
    • Counts and sums are recomputed from the transactions, in integer cents, for each block and for the group header, and compared with NbOfTxs and CtrlSum.
    • IBAN uses the mod-97 check and the country's fixed length. A failing IBAN is reported with the check digits that would pass if only they were wrong, but nothing is ever changed for you.
    • Execution dates on a Saturday, Sunday, Good Friday, Easter Monday, 1 May, 25 or 26 December are flagged with the next banking day.
    • Rebuild rewrites NbOfTxs and CtrlSum only. It never edits a payment, an IBAN, an amount or a name.
    • Not checked: your bank's schema list, limits and cut-off times, whether a BIC matches its IBAN, sanctions screening, instant payments, direct debits (pain.008), non-euro and international payments, and anything your bank adds to the EPC rules.

    Common questions

    How do I check a SEPA payment file before I upload it to my bank?

    Paste the pain.001 XML or drop the file onto this page. It checks the XML structure, the group header and payment blocks, every IBAN with the mod-97 check, the transaction count and control sum at both levels, the execution date against weekends and TARGET2 closing days, the euro currency and amount format, and the characters allowed in names and references, then lists each problem with its line number.

    Why was my SEPA XML file rejected with a control sum or NbOfTxs error?

    The group header and every payment block repeat the number of transactions and the sum of the amounts. After someone edits an amount or deletes a payee by hand, those two numbers no longer match what the file holds and the bank refuses it. This tool recomputes both and can rewrite just those fields.

    How is an IBAN checked?

    Move the first four characters to the end, turn letters into numbers (A is 10, B is 11 and so on), and divide the long number by 97. A valid IBAN leaves a remainder of 1. The country also fixes the length, for example 22 characters for Germany and 18 for the Netherlands. The check catches a mistyped or swapped character; it cannot tell you the account belongs to the person you meant to pay.

    Why does the bank complain about a character in the payee name?

    The basic SEPA character set is the letters a to z without accents, digits and the symbols / - ? : ( ) . , ' + and space. Accented letters, an ampersand and many other symbols fall outside it. Some banks transliterate them and some reject the whole file.

    Can this tool fix my SEPA file?

    It can recompute NbOfTxs and CtrlSum in the group header and each payment block, which is what is wrong after a hand edit. It never edits a payment: a wrong IBAN, amount or name is a payment decision, so it is reported and left to you.

    Is it safe to put a file with bank account numbers into a web page?

    The page runs in your browser, the file is read locally and nothing is uploaded; a test in the code asserts there are no network calls. Account numbers are masked to their last four characters in the report and the downloaded findings list. Your own policies still decide whether you may open a payment file in a browser.

    What does this not check?

    Whether your bank accepts your schema version, your daily limits and cut-off times, whether the creditor's BIC matches the IBAN, sanctions screening, instant-payment (SCT Inst) limits, direct debit (pain.008) files, non-euro and international payment layouts, and any rule your bank adds on top of the EPC scheme. A clean result is not a promise of acceptance.

    No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, banking, payments, compliance, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional or your bank's own validation. Results depend entirely on the file you provide. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it, including with your bank before you send a payment file, and a clean result is not a promise that a bank will accept the file.

    Not affiliated with the European Payments Council or any bank. SEPA, ISO 20022 and TARGET2 are names of their respective owners. This tool is independent and is not sponsored, endorsed or connected to the European Payments Council, the ECB, ISO, or any bank or payment processor. The rules are read from memory of the public documents and may not match every bank's variant.

    Payment data. SEPA files contain IBANs and the names of the people or companies you pay. This page runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere, and the portfolio never receives your file. Whether you may open a payment file in a browser tool is a question for your own security policies.

    Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

    Everything runs in your browser. Your file is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (file_validated, example_loaded, controls_rebuilt) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

    Related tools: the NACHA file validator does the same job for US ACH files, the duplicate payment audit finds the invoice you paid twice, and the 1099 vendor tracker keeps the vendors you pay in one list. Reading the statement file your bank sends back? The BAI2 statement reader turns it into a table and checks its totals.
